title: GENIE - Genetic Information and Education_Study 1
summary: Rare genetic disorders often manifest as early as childhood and present affected families with many new questions and uncertainties. Especially following a diagnosis, it is important to convey medical information in an understandable way so that patients and their families can better understand the condition and cope with the challenges it presents. The GENIE (Genetic Information and Education) research project examines how information can be conveyed in a way that is understandable and patient-centered during human genetic counseling. The project consists of two substudies. In the first substudy, physicians who provide genetic counseling are surveyed online about their experiences. Among other things, the survey examines which factors facilitate or hinder understandable counseling, what difficulties arise when conveying complex genetic information, and what additional support services might be helpful from a physician’s perspective.

interventions.name: Physicians authorized to provide human genetic counseling will be surveyed once via an online questionnaire regarding barriers, factors contributing to success, and support needs in genetic counseling.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Physicians who are authorized to provide genetic counseling in accordance with the guidelines of the Genetic Diagnostics Commission
(GEKO); Sufficient proficiency in German; Reliable internet access
Exclusion criteria:
None
